# cross

Consider the two accounts together. Explore disagreements, shared assumptions, or a different problem their relationship brings into view, where the content gives you grounds.

## Original problem (task)
[5e2851f2d1f5e1aa] (h005.task.v1)
I share a flat with two friends. We keep arguing about ordinary household chores. Sometimes we agree on who will do something, but later we disagree about what the agreement meant. Our work schedules change, and one friend has started avoiding the conversations. What should I do?

BODY
This contribution is an assembly-and-pressure-test node. I was not handed any earlier commitment field, so I can only work with the prose handed to me: the carry's admission that its second observational track is weak against rival readings, the note that the source's first template invocation left the origin absent, and the load-bearing commitments the carry identifies (k6: don't open the separate conversation with a household-ontology question; k8: if neither axis moves, name the living-arrangement question directly; k9: flag the silence about whether the withdrawing person will utter any commitment-tinged sentence).

What I can add that the carry did not: examine whether the two-track probe the carry proposes is *observable in principle* under the constraints the carry itself asserts, and whether the stop condition is actually reachable.

First, the stop condition. The carry says: run the one-item probe, watch recurrence and content-vs-form for two or three weeks, and if neither axis produces a signal, treat that as the chore frame not being where the friction lives. This is coherent only if 'neither axis produces a signal' is a determinate outcome rather than a residual category. But consider: recurrence is quantitative and can silently drift (a flatmate does a chore late but does do it — does that register as 'recurrence fell'?); content-vs-form is categor-ical and depends on whether any sentence with a commitment appears at all. The carry's own k9 admits the second track is silent on the very evidence it needs. So the stop condition may be triggered not by a clean null but by an unclassifiable pattern — e.g., recurrence holds steady while the withdrawing flatmate still deflects any commitment-shaped utterance. That pattern is not 'neither axis moved'; it is 'one axis moved and the other is unreadable because its instrument is broken.' The carry does not say what to do with that pattern, and I do not think the evidence in front of me supplies it.

Second, the voice problem. The withdrawing flatmate has started avoiding the conversations. The probe requires a conversation — the one-item probe is an intervention, not a passive observation. If the withdrawal is from the *form* of arrangement-talk (rival's axis) then even the one-item probe may trigger more withdrawal; if it is from any obligation-talk, the probe is the obligation. Either way, the act of probing is itself load-bearing on the outcome, and the carry does not name that reflexivity. This is not a fatal objection to running the probe; it is a reason the probe's result cannot be read as a neutral measurement.

Third, the origin absence. The carry says the origin is absent from the first template invocation and it will not pretend otherwise. I have no more access than the carry does. I note only that this absence has an interpretive consequence the carry does not spell out: if the origin contained a statement of what the flatmates originally agreed to (as opposed to what each now remembers agreeing to), then the carry's whole framing of 'we disagree about what the agreement meant' would be measuring against a moving baseline, and the probe's design would need to be different. Without the origin, the only defensible position is the one the carry already occupies: assess relative to the materials in hand, and flag that a later invocation with origin access might need to reintroduce it.

Fourth, on what to do. I would preserve the carry's k6, k8, k9 without revision. I would add: (a) run the one-item probe, but name in advance that the probe is an intervention that may alter the pattern it measures; (b) when the two-week or three-week mark arrives, classify the result into at least four cells, not two: neither axis moves / recurrence-falls-only / content-vs-form-unreadable-only / both-move; (c) treat 'content-vs-form-unreadable-only' as the trigger for the living-arrangement conversation (k8), not as a null result; (d) if both-move, continue the current arrangement without escalation but re-probe at the next schedule change.

I do not know whether this is better than the carry. It is a different pressure point — reflexivity of the probe, and the stop condition's hidden fourth cell. If the next node can supply the origin or a flatmate's own account of the withdrawal, that would discipline cells (a) and (c) more than any refinement of the probe's wording can.

BODY
I have only the commitments record from the prior node; the prior prose body is not in front of me, and neither is the origin that p.carry.3 reportedly failed to fetch. So I should say plainly what that costs me before saying anything useful about the flat.

The prior record already does the honest work of marking its own limits: it declines to treat a pullback-from-form observation as settling the unit-versus-privacy question (n1, n4), and it says the discriminating fact is not about chores but about whether the withdrawing flatmate will say anything commitment-shaped at all (n2). That second point is the one I find most load-bearing for the actual question, because the original problem describes a household where agreements are made and then re-described differently, schedules shift, and one person has stopped showing up to the conversations. Every one of those is a communication-condition problem before it is a chores problem.

What the prior record does not do, and what I cannot do from here without inventing, is tell you what the chores are, how long this has run, whether the withdrawing flatmate has given any reason, or whether the other two flatmates agree with each other about what happened. Those are listed as missing (n5) and they remain missing to me. I will not fabricate a third track of observation to close the gap.

So my contribution is a narrowing, not a solution. Three things follow from the material I can see:

First, the dispute you describe is not well-modeled as disagreement about who does what. It is well-modeled as disagreement about what a prior utterance committed anyone to. That is a different failure mode, and it has different remedies. Re-allocating chores will not fix a household where the same sentence can be read two ways after the fact, because the next agreement will drift the same way.

Second, the withdrawal is itself the most informative signal available, and it is underdetermined. The prior record is right that pullback-from-form is compatible with at least three readings: that the withdrawing flatmate wants the arrangement kept private or informal, that they are avoiding obligation, and that they are resentful about load and have stopped voicing it. I cannot tell these apart from here. What I can say is that a plan which assumes the obligation-avoidance reading will, if that reading is wrong, convert a communication problem into a grievance. A plan which assumes the privacy reading will under-ask and let the drift continue. That is not an argument for choosing one; it is an argument for a move that survives both readings.

Third, no move I can recommend is fully licensed by the evidence I have. What the evidence supports is a move whose main virtue is that it generates the missing information rather than acting as if it were already in hand. That is the whole content of my recommendation: not a division of labor, but a low-cost, low-commitment way to make the drift visible.

Concretely, the shape I would suggest, held with the caveats above: name the pattern, not the person. Say that the recurring problem is disagreements about what past agreements meant, and propose a single written record of who agreed to what and by when, kept somewhere all three can see, without enforcement attached. The point is not surveillance; it is that the shared record is the missing observation, and it can only be made by the household from inside, not inferred by me from outside. If the withdrawing flatmate will engage with that at all, you have learned something n2 says is currently unavailable. If they will not, you have learned that too, and the reading is still open between privacy and avoidance and resentment.

I want to be explicit about what I am not claiming. I am not claiming this resolves the ambiguity, or that it will bring the withdrawing flatmate back into the conversation, or that it is the best move for this specific household. I do not know this household. I know that the prior record's honest ceiling (n1, n5) is the correct ceiling, that my proposal sits under it, and that anything stronger I said about it would be me supplying facts I do not have. The prior node's commitment n8 also applies to me: if origin material surfaces later, whatever in it bears on whether the prior carry's shape was warranted should be read, not silently absorbed.
COMMITMENTS
